summary: A dense, systems-heavy Pfister design where you route specialists across a hex map to fulfill ever-shifting resource needs while managing a bag/deck of tokens and riding a day/night rondel. It rewards efficient engine-building and planning several turns ahead more than reacting to opponents, with real weight in tracking multiple interlocking subsystems.
praised: Deep, satisfying puzzle of resource and route optimization
Strong solo mode that holds up on repeated plays
High replayability from varied need cards and map routes
Thematic day/night and blackout mechanisms feel well integrated
criticised: Steep learning curve and fiddly rules overhead
Long turns and downtime, especially at higher player counts
Theme is thin dressing over a dense Euro engine

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with light competition for map routes and shared resources

scoring.why: Points accumulate from fulfilling need cards, route/network building, and end-game bonuses, so the winner is whoever built the most efficient overall engine rather than one dominant strategy
